name: Triangle porch
_about: A PORCH ON A TRIANGULAR PLAN before a portal (Regensburg's Dreieckportal, c. 1410): its back is the wall it stands against (from x = -half to half on z = 0), its tip `depth` out on +z, where ONE PILLAR carries the two front faces. Each face is a wall `w` long, open in a pointed arch (`pier` of wall either side, springing at `spring`) and only `h` high -- just over the arch's crown; over it a crocketed GABLE (wimperg) stands FREE, its tracery open to the sky, up to `gableTop` at most (steeper or flatter by `pitch`). A slab closes the porch at `h`, a pierced parapet runs along the faces' heads behind the gables, pinnacles stand on its back corners and a tall one over the pillar. `w` and `yaw` (the faces' length and turn) follow from half and depth. Place it with its back on the wall's face, facing +z.

params._yaw: the right face's turn (a yaw turns +x towards -z); the left one's is its negative
params._h: the faces' walls: just over the arches' crowns (an equilateral arch rises 0.866 of its width)
params._gableTop: the most the gables may rise to: wimperg.js flattens a gable that would rise higher, and drops one it cannot fit
params._tipW: the pinnacle over the pillar (tipW, tipH, tipS); pinW, pinH, pinS the back corners'

faces._about: the two front faces, each open in a pointed arch under its free-standing gable (their outer faces on the triangle's sides)

pillar._about: the one pillar at the tip, which both arches spring from

slab._about: the porch's head: a slab over its vault, the faces' tops

parapet._about: a pierced parapet along each face's head, on the wall behind its gable

tip pinnacle._about: the tall pinnacle over the pillar
